backlog.summary: First backlog draft for a digital absence reporting solution piloted at Lindenhof primary school (Canton of St. Gallen, fictional). The main risk to address is children who are missing without a report, because the school has a duty of care. Parents want to report absences on their phone in under a minute, including the evening before, and receive a confirmation. Phone reports to the school office must still be possible and are entered into the same system. Absence reasons are limited to categories, with no medical details. Planned absences follow an approval workflow: the class teacher approves up to two days and the principal approves longer absences. Teachers take attendance per lesson on a tablet. The school office is alerted when an absent child has no parent report. Absence counts per semester feed the report card. Student, class, parent and custody data come from the canton's student administration system. The parent-facing parts must be multilingual. Data retention and the interface details still need to be confirmed with the canton's data protection officer and IT department.

personas.name: Parent
personas.description: Parent or legal guardian of a pupil. Often starts work early and wants to report absences from their phone quickly, ideally the evening before. Some families have limited German skills or do not use smartphones. Represented by Peter Graf (Parent Council).

personas.name: Class teacher
personas.description: Teacher responsible for a class (e.g. Aylin Demir, 4th grade). Takes attendance, needs to see all absences of the class in one place, and approves planned absences of up to two days. Must not receive medical details. Does not want absence messages on a private phone.

personas.name: Subject teacher
personas.description: Teacher who teaches a pupil in specific lessons on a given day (e.g. sports teacher). Needs to know which of their pupils are absent that day.

personas.name: School office staff
personas.description: Staff at the school office. Receives phone calls from parents, needs an overview of all absences, and contacts families when a child is missing without a report.

personas.name: Principal
personas.description: School principal (Thomas Brunner). Responsible for the duty of care, approves planned absences longer than two days, and is accountable for compliance with custody restrictions and data protection.

epics.title: Absence reporting
epics.goal: Parents and the school office can record absences quickly in one system, using structured reasons and no medical details, so that the school knows why a child is absent.

epics.title: Planned absence requests and approval
epics.goal: Parents can request planned absences in advance and the correct approver (class teacher or principal) decides, with the status visible to parents.

epics.title: Attendance taking and missing-child alerts
epics.goal: Teachers record attendance per lesson and the school office is alerted about absent children without a parent report, so families can be contacted promptly.

epics.title: Absence visibility and report card figures
epics.goal: Class teachers, subject teachers and the school office see the absences relevant to them, and semester absence counts for the report card are calculated automatically.

epics.title: Master data, custody and access
epics.goal: Student, class, parent and custody data are taken from the canton's student administration system, and information is shared only with authorised persons.

epics.title: Multilingual parent experience
epics.goal: Parents with limited German can use the reporting features in the school's main languages.

stories.title: Report a sickness absence on the phone
stories.i_want: to report my child's absence on my phone by selecting the child, the days and a reason
stories.so_that: I don't have to call the busy office line before work
stories.statement: As a parent, I want to report my child's absence on my phone by selecting the child, the days and a reason, so that I don't have to call the busy office line before work.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am logged in as a parent with one or more children at the school
acceptance_criteria.when: I start a new absence report
acceptance_criteria.then: I can select only my own children, one or more absence days, and one reason category

acceptance_criteria.given: I have filled in child, days and reason
acceptance_criteria.then: the absence is saved and becomes visible to the child's class teacher

acceptance_criteria.given: I have not selected a child, a day or a reason
acceptance_criteria.when: I try to submit the report
acceptance_criteria.then: submission is blocked and the missing field is indicated

stories.priority_rationale: Parent self-reporting is the core of the solution and directly addresses the frustration with the busy office line.
source_quotes: calling at 7:15 when the office line is busy is frustrating
I'd like to report it on my phone in a minute
Which child, which days, and roughly the reason.
stories.notes: Depends on US-18 (student and parent data import). The reason list is defined in US-3. Target duration: see NFR-3.

stories.title: Report an absence the evening before
stories.i_want: to report an absence for the next school day in advance, e.g. the evening before
stories.so_that: I don't have to report it early in the morning when I already know the day before
stories.statement: As a parent, I want to report an absence for the next school day in advance, e.g. the evening before, so that I don't have to report it early in the morning when I already know the day before.

acceptance_criteria.given: it is the evening before a school day
acceptance_criteria.when: I submit a sickness absence for the next school day
acceptance_criteria.then: the report is accepted and appears for that day in the class teacher's view

acceptance_criteria.given: I reported an absence for the next day
acceptance_criteria.when: the teacher takes attendance the next morning
acceptance_criteria.then: the child is shown as reported absent

stories.priority_rationale: The parent representative explicitly asked for it, but same-day reporting (US-1) delivers the core value first.
source_quotes: ideally the evening before if I already know
Many of us start work early.
stories.notes: Can be delivered as an extension of US-1. Clarify how far ahead a sickness report may be made, as opposed to a planned absence request (US-6).

stories.title: Select a reason category instead of entering medical details
stories.i_want: absence reasons to be limited to predefined categories such as sick, doctor's appointment and family reason
stories.so_that: I know roughly why a child is absent without receiving medical details
stories.statement: As a class teacher, I want absence reasons to be limited to predefined categories such as sick, doctor's appointment and family reason, so that I know roughly why a child is absent without receiving medical details.

acceptance_criteria.given: a parent or office staff member reports an absence
acceptance_criteria.then: they can choose only from the predefined categories, including sick, doctor's appointment and family reason

acceptance_criteria.given: the absence report form
acceptance_criteria.then: it contains no free-text field for describing the reason

acceptance_criteria.given: an absence has been reported
acceptance_criteria.when: I view it as class teacher
acceptance_criteria.then: I see the reason category only

stories.priority_rationale: The principal and the teacher both stated that medical details must not be collected, which is a data protection requirement.
source_quotes: Sick, doctor's appointment, family reason. I don't need medical details.
Actually I shouldn't get medical details.
Health data is sensitive.
stories.notes: Related to NFR-1. The final category list (e.g. accident) is to be confirmed. See open questions.

stories.title: Receive a confirmation of the report
stories.i_want: to receive a confirmation after submitting an absence report
stories.so_that: I know the school has received it
stories.statement: As a parent, I want to receive a confirmation after submitting an absence report, so that I know the school has received it.

acceptance_criteria.given: I have submitted an absence report
acceptance_criteria.then: I see a confirmation showing the child, the days and the reason category

acceptance_criteria.given: I have submitted an absence report
acceptance_criteria.when: I open my list of reports
acceptance_criteria.then: the report is listed with the status 'received'

stories.priority_rationale: The parent representative named the confirmation as part of the success criteria.
source_quotes: That reporting takes less than a minute and I get a confirmation.
stories.notes: Depends on US-1. The confirmation channel (in-app, e-mail, push) is still open.

stories.title: Office enters phone-reported absences
stories.i_want: to enter absences that parents report by phone into the same system
stories.so_that: teachers see all absences in one place, regardless of how they were reported
stories.statement: As school office staff, I want to enter absences that parents report by phone into the same system, so that teachers see all absences in one place, regardless of how they were reported.

acceptance_criteria.given: a parent calls the office to report an absence
acceptance_criteria.when: I enter the child, the days and the reason category
acceptance_criteria.then: the absence is saved and visible to the class teacher, just like an app report

acceptance_criteria.given: an absence was entered by the office
acceptance_criteria.then: it is marked as reported by phone via the office

acceptance_criteria.given: I search for a pupil
acceptance_criteria.when: I type part of the name
acceptance_criteria.then: I can select the pupil from the imported student list

stories.priority_rationale: The principal stated that phone calls must remain possible because not everyone will use an app.
source_quotes: And phone calls must still be possible.
If a parent calls the office, the office should enter it in the same system, so I see everything in one place.
stories.notes: Depends on US-18. Reuses the reason categories from US-3.

stories.title: Request a planned absence in advance
stories.i_want: to request a planned absence, such as a family wedding, in advance
stories.so_that: the school can approve it before the absence takes place
stories.statement: As a parent, I want to request a planned absence, such as a family wedding, in advance, so that the school can approve it before the absence takes place.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am logged in as a parent
acceptance_criteria.when: I create a planned absence request with child, future dates and reason category
acceptance_criteria.then: the request is saved with the status 'pending'

acceptance_criteria.given: I try to create a planned absence request
acceptance_criteria.when: the selected start date is in the past
acceptance_criteria.then: the request is rejected with a message that planned absences must be requested in advance

stories.priority_rationale: The principal described planned absences as a distinct absence type that must be requested in advance.
source_quotes: Then there are planned absences, like a family wedding, which parents have to request in advance.
stories.notes: Routing to the approver is handled in US-7 and US-8. The minimum lead time is unclear.

stories.title: Class teacher approves short planned absences
stories.i_want: to approve or reject planned absence requests of up to two days for my class
stories.so_that: short absences can be decided without involving the principal
stories.statement: As a class teacher, I want to approve or reject planned absence requests of up to two days for my class, so that short absences can be decided without involving the principal.

acceptance_criteria.given: a parent submits a planned absence request of two days or less for a pupil in my class
acceptance_criteria.then: it appears in my list of requests to decide

acceptance_criteria.given: a pending request of two days or less
acceptance_criteria.then: the status changes to 'approved' or 'rejected' and the parent can see the new status

acceptance_criteria.given: a planned absence request of more than two days
acceptance_criteria.then: it does not appear in my list of requests to decide

stories.priority_rationale: The principal defined this approval rule explicitly as part of the current process.
source_quotes: Up to two days the class teacher can approve.
stories.notes: Depends on US-6. It is open whether 'two days' means school days or calendar days, and how half-days count.

stories.title: Principal approves longer planned absences
stories.i_want: to approve or reject planned absence requests longer than two days
stories.so_that: longer absences are decided at the level required by school rules
stories.statement: As a principal, I want to approve or reject planned absence requests longer than two days, so that longer absences are decided at the level required by school rules.

acceptance_criteria.given: a parent submits a planned absence request of more than two days
acceptance_criteria.then: it appears in the principal's list of requests to decide

acceptance_criteria.given: a pending request of more than two days
acceptance_criteria.then: the status changes accordingly and is visible to the parent and the class teacher

stories.priority_rationale: The principal stated that absences longer than two days require his approval.
source_quotes: Longer than that, I have to approve as principal.
stories.notes: Depends on US-6. Should the class teacher be informed of or comment on the request? To be clarified.

stories.title: See the approver and the approval status
stories.i_want: to see who needs to approve my planned absence request and whether it has been approved
stories.so_that: I understand the rules and know whether my child may be absent
stories.statement: As a parent, I want to see who needs to approve my planned absence request and whether it has been approved, so that I understand the rules and know whether my child may be absent.

acceptance_criteria.given: I have submitted a planned absence request
acceptance_criteria.then: I see the responsible approver role (class teacher or principal) and the current status (pending, approved or rejected)

acceptance_criteria.given: my request has been decided
acceptance_criteria.then: I receive a notification with the decision

stories.priority_rationale: The parent representative noted that nobody knows the rules today. Status transparency adds clear value, but it builds on US-6 to US-8.
source_quotes: right now nobody knows the rules
I'd like the app to tell me who needs to approve and whether it was approved.
stories.notes: Depends on US-6, US-7 and US-8.

stories.title: Take attendance per lesson on a tablet
stories.i_want: to mark which pupils are present at the start of each lesson on my tablet
stories.so_that: absences are recorded without paper lists
stories.statement: As a class teacher, I want to mark which pupils are present at the start of each lesson on my tablet, so that absences are recorded without paper lists.

acceptance_criteria.given: I open the attendance view on my tablet for my current lesson
acceptance_criteria.then: all pupils of the class are listed, and pupils with a reported or approved absence are marked as such

acceptance_criteria.given: the attendance list for a class of 24 pupils
acceptance_criteria.when: I mark the absent pupils and save
acceptance_criteria.then: the attendance for that lesson is stored, with each pupil marked present or absent

acceptance_criteria.given: a class of 24 pupils with all present by default
acceptance_criteria.then: the task can be completed in under one minute (see NFR-4)

stories.priority_rationale: Attendance data is the basis for detecting missing children, which the principal named as the biggest concern.
source_quotes: At the start of each lesson I'd check who's there.
It has to work on my tablet in under a minute, otherwise I won't do it with 24 kids waiting.
stories.notes: Clarify whether subject teachers also take attendance in their lessons. Pre-marking reported absences depends on US-1 and US-5.

stories.title: Alert the office about unreported absences
stories.i_want: to be alerted when a child is marked absent and there is no report from the parents
stories.so_that: I can call the family and the school fulfils its duty of care
stories.statement: As school office staff, I want to be alerted when a child is marked absent and there is no report from the parents, so that I can call the family and the school fulfils its duty of care.

acceptance_criteria.given: a teacher marks a pupil absent
acceptance_criteria.when: no absence report or approved planned absence exists for that pupil and day
acceptance_criteria.then: an alert with the pupil's name, class and parent contact details is shown to the school office

acceptance_criteria.given: a pupil is marked absent and has a reported absence
acceptance_criteria.then: no alert is created

acceptance_criteria.given: an open alert
acceptance_criteria.when: office staff record that the family has been contacted
acceptance_criteria.then: the alert is marked as resolved, with the time and the staff member

stories.priority_rationale: The principal called unreported absences the biggest concern and the key success criterion.
source_quotes: That's actually our biggest concern.
And if a child is marked absent but there's no report from the parents, the school office should be alerted so they can call the family.
That we know about every missing child within thirty minutes of the first lesson.
stories.notes: Depends on US-10 and US-1/US-5. Time target: see NFR-6. Parent contact details must respect custody restrictions (US-19).

stories.title: Notify parents when the child does not arrive
stories.i_want: to receive a notification if my child is marked absent without a report
stories.so_that: I have peace of mind and can react immediately
stories.statement: As a parent, I want to receive a notification if my child is marked absent without a report, so that I have peace of mind and can react immediately.

acceptance_criteria.given: my child is marked absent and no absence has been reported
acceptance_criteria.then: I receive a notification that my child has not arrived, provided I am authorised to receive information about the child

acceptance_criteria.given: a parent is not authorised to receive information about the child under a custody arrangement
acceptance_criteria.when: the child is marked absent without a report
acceptance_criteria.then: no notification is sent to that parent

stories.priority_rationale: The parent representative requested it, but the principal warned about custody restrictions, so it depends on reliable custody data.
source_quotes: I'd want a notification if my child doesn't arrive.
The system must respect custody arrangements.
stories.notes: Depends on US-19 and US-18. Point of tension between the parent representative and the principal: see open questions.

stories.title: Class teacher sees all absences of the class
stories.i_want: to see all reported, planned and recorded absences of my class in one place
stories.so_that: I no longer have to collect them from calls and private messages
stories.statement: As a class teacher, I want to see all reported, planned and recorded absences of my class in one place, so that I no longer have to collect them from calls and private messages.

acceptance_criteria.given: absences have been reported via the app or by the office
acceptance_criteria.when: I open my class overview for a day
acceptance_criteria.then: I see each absent pupil with the days, the reason category and the reporting channel

acceptance_criteria.given: I am a class teacher
acceptance_criteria.then: I see only pupils of my own class

stories.priority_rationale: The teacher explicitly wants everything in one place instead of messages on her private phone.
source_quotes: The class teacher, obviously.
or they send me a message on my private phone, which I really don't like.

stories.title: Subject teacher sees absences of the day
stories.i_want: to see which of the pupils I teach on a given day are absent
stories.so_that: I can plan my lesson, e.g. sports, accordingly
stories.statement: As a subject teacher, I want to see which of the pupils I teach on a given day are absent, so that I can plan my lesson, e.g. sports, accordingly.

acceptance_criteria.given: I teach a pupil on a given day
acceptance_criteria.when: that pupil has an absence for that day
acceptance_criteria.then: the pupil is shown as absent in my view for that day

acceptance_criteria.given: a pupil I do not teach on that day is absent
acceptance_criteria.then: that pupil is not shown

stories.priority_rationale: Explicitly mentioned by the class teacher, but secondary to the class teacher and office views.
source_quotes: And the subject teachers who have the child that day, like the sports teacher.
stories.notes: Requires timetable or lesson assignment data. It is unclear whether the canton system provides this: see open questions.

stories.title: Office overview of all absences
stories.i_want: an overview of all absences across the school for a selected day
stories.so_that: I have a complete picture of who is absent
stories.statement: As school office staff, I want an overview of all absences across the school for a selected day, so that I have a complete picture of who is absent.

acceptance_criteria.given: absences exist in several classes
acceptance_criteria.when: I open the overview for a date
acceptance_criteria.then: I see all absent pupils of all classes with class, reason category and status (reported, approved, unreported)

acceptance_criteria.given: the overview
acceptance_criteria.then: only absences of that class are shown

stories.priority_rationale: The teacher stated that the office needs an overview of all absences, and this view is needed to follow up on missing children.
source_quotes: The school office needs an overview of all absences.

stories.title: Semester absence count for the report card
stories.i_want: the system to calculate the number of absences per pupil for the semester
stories.so_that: I no longer have to count them by hand for the report card
stories.statement: As a class teacher, I want the system to calculate the number of absences per pupil for the semester, so that I no longer have to count them by hand for the report card.

acceptance_criteria.given: absences have been recorded during a semester
acceptance_criteria.when: I open the semester summary for my class
acceptance_criteria.then: I see the total number of absences per pupil for that semester

acceptance_criteria.given: a pupil had three recorded absences in the semester
acceptance_criteria.then: the count shown for that pupil is 3, in the unit agreed for the report card

stories.priority_rationale: The principal named manual counting as error-prone, but it is needed only at the end of the semester and depends on the core recording features.
source_quotes: And at the end of the semester the number of absences goes on the report card.
Today the teachers count them by hand from their lists. That's error-prone.
stories.notes: Counting unit (days, half-days, lessons) and excused/unexcused split to be clarified. Export to a report card system is not mentioned.

stories.title: Import students, classes and parents from the canton system
stories.i_want: classes, students and parents to be taken from the canton's student administration system
stories.so_that: nobody has to enter students manually
stories.statement: As a principal, I want classes, students and parents to be taken from the canton's student administration system, so that nobody has to enter students manually.

acceptance_criteria.given: the interface to the canton's student administration system is configured
acceptance_criteria.then: classes, students and parent relationships are created or updated in the absence system

acceptance_criteria.given: a student exists in the canton system
acceptance_criteria.when: office staff look for that student
acceptance_criteria.then: the student is available without manual entry

acceptance_criteria.given: the absence system
acceptance_criteria.when: a user tries to create a student manually
acceptance_criteria.then: no such function is available

stories.priority_rationale: The principal explicitly ruled out manual student entry, and all other features rely on this data.
source_quotes: the canton's student administration system has all the classes, students and parents.
We should not enter students manually.
stories.notes: Blocked until the canton IT department describes the interface. Sync frequency is unknown.

stories.title: Parent access based on imported parent relationships
stories.i_want: to log in and see only my own children as imported from the canton system
stories.so_that: I can report absences without registering my children myself
stories.statement: As a parent, I want to log in and see only my own children as imported from the canton system, so that I can report absences without registering my children myself.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am recorded as a parent of a child in the canton system
acceptance_criteria.then: I see that child and can report absences for them

acceptance_criteria.given: a child is not linked to me in the canton system
acceptance_criteria.then: I cannot see or report absences for that child

stories.priority_rationale: Parent reporting (US-1) requires a reliable link between parents and children, which the principal said comes from the canton system.
source_quotes: the canton's student administration system has all the classes, students and parents.
stories.notes: Depends on US-17. The authentication method for parents is not discussed: see open questions.

stories.title: Respect custody restrictions
stories.i_want: custody restrictions from the canton's student database to control which parents receive information about a child
stories.so_that: the school complies with legal restrictions in cases such as divorced parents
stories.statement: As a principal, I want custody restrictions from the canton's student database to control which parents receive information about a child, so that the school complies with legal restrictions in cases such as divorced parents.

acceptance_criteria.given: a parent is flagged in the canton database as not entitled to receive information about a child
acceptance_criteria.when: absence information or notifications about that child are produced
acceptance_criteria.then: that parent receives none of them and cannot view the child's absences

acceptance_criteria.given: a custody restriction changes in the canton database
acceptance_criteria.then: the access rights in the absence system reflect the change

stories.priority_rationale: The principal stated this as a legal obligation the system must meet.
source_quotes: we sometimes have legal restrictions on who gets information.
The system must respect custody arrangements.
We get those from the canton's student database.
stories.notes: Depends on US-17. Prerequisite for US-12.

stories.title: Use the parent app in my language
stories.i_want: to use the absence reporting features in my language
stories.so_that: I can report absences even if I don't speak German well
stories.statement: As a parent, I want to use the absence reporting features in my language, so that I can report absences even if I don't speak German well.

acceptance_criteria.given: I open the parent app
acceptance_criteria.when: I select a language from the supported list
acceptance_criteria.then: all labels, reason categories, confirmations and notifications are shown in that language

acceptance_criteria.given: the release scope
acceptance_criteria.then: at least German and English are available, with Albanian, Portuguese and Tigrinya added if confirmed

stories.priority_rationale: The parent representative warned that families won't use a German-only app, and the principal named minimum languages.
source_quotes: If the app is only in German, they won't use it.
but at least German, English, and maybe Albanian, Portuguese and Tigrinya
stories.notes: Can be split per language. Avoiding free text (US-3) simplifies translation. The final language list needs confirmation.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The system must not collect medical details about absences. Reasons are captured only as predefined categories, and no free-text reason field may be offered to parents.
source_quotes: Health data is sensitive.
Actually I shouldn't get medical details.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Absence totals needed for the report card must be retained. Daily absence details are expected to be deleted after the school year. The final retention periods must be confirmed with the canton's data protection officer before go-live.
source_quotes: Absence data for the report card has to be kept
I'd guess they should be deleted after the school year
Please check that with the canton's data protection officer.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: A parent must be able to complete an absence report on a smartphone in less than one minute.
source_quotes: I'd like to report it on my phone in a minute
That reporting takes less than a minute

non_functional_requirements.requirement: A teacher must be able to record attendance for a class of 24 pupils on a tablet in under one minute.
source_quotes: It has to work on my tablet in under a minute, otherwise I won't do it with 24 kids waiting.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The school must know about every child missing without a report within thirty minutes of the first lesson. Unreported-absence alerts must reach the school office early enough to meet this target.
source_quotes: That we know about every missing child within thirty minutes of the first lesson.
We need to reach the parents within the first hour of school.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Access to absence data must be role-based. Class teachers see their class, subject teachers see the pupils they teach that day, the office sees all absences, and parents see only children they are legally entitled to receive information about.
source_quotes: The system must respect custody arrangements.
The school office needs an overview of all absences.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The canton's student administration system is the source for classes, students, parents and custody arrangements. The interface is to be specified by the canton's IT department.
source_quotes: We should not enter students manually.
The IT department of the canton would need to tell you how the interface works.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The parent-facing user interface must be multilingual, with at least German and English. Albanian, Portuguese and Tigrinya are candidates for the school's biggest language groups.
source_quotes: At our school we have more than twenty languages.
but at least German, English, and maybe Albanian, Portuguese and Tigrinya

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Phone reporting via the school office must remain a supported channel alongside the app, so that families without a smartphone or app can still report absences.
source_quotes: And phone calls must still be possible.
Not everyone will use an app.

open_questions.question: How does the interface to the canton's student administration system work: protocol, sync frequency, and the data fields available (including custody flags and timetables)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: All core features depend on this master data. Subject teacher views also need lesson assignments.

open_questions.question: What are the legally required retention periods for daily absence details and for report card absence totals?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The principal only guessed at deletion after the school year. The retention rules determine the deletion jobs and the data model.

open_questions.question: Is the target to detect missing children within thirty minutes of the first lesson or within the first hour of school? The principal mentioned both.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The time target drives the alert timing and the acceptance criteria for US-11.

open_questions.question: The parent representative wants automatic notifications when a child doesn't arrive, while the principal warned about custody restrictions. Should notifications be sent at all, to whom, and should they be opt-in?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is a potential conflict between stakeholders with legal implications.
open_questions.ask_whom: Thomas Brunner (Principal), Peter Graf (Parent Council), canton data protection officer

open_questions.question: Does 'up to two days' for class teacher approval refer to school days or calendar days, and how are half-days handled?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This defines the routing rule between the class teacher and the principal.

open_questions.question: What is the minimum lead time for planned absence requests, and what happens if a request has not been decided before the absence date?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Validation and escalation rules for the approval workflow depend on it.

open_questions.question: What is the complete list of reason categories (e.g. is 'accident' a separate category), and do subject teachers see the reason or only that the pupil is absent?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The reason list affects data protection and the translated content.

open_questions.question: In which unit are absences counted for the report card (days, half-days, lessons), and are excused and unexcused absences counted separately?
open_questions.why_it_matters: US-16 cannot be specified or tested without this.

open_questions.question: Do subject teachers also take attendance in their own lessons, or does only the class teacher take attendance?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This affects alert logic and data volume, and determines who triggers unreported-absence alerts.

open_questions.question: The question about families without smartphones was answered mainly with respect to language. Is a web version for desktop computers, or another channel (e.g. SMS), needed besides the phone call to the office?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This determines the channel scope for the pilot.

open_questions.question: Which languages are confirmed for the pilot? Albanian, Portuguese and Tigrinya were mentioned only as 'maybe'. Who provides the translations?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This affects scope, cost and timeline.

open_questions.question: Which accessibility standard (e.g. WCAG 2.1 AA / eCH-0059) must the solution meet?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Accessibility was not discussed but is typically mandatory for public-sector software.

open_questions.question: How do parents and staff authenticate (e.g. cantonal login, e-mail account)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Login is a prerequisite for parent reporting and affects security.

open_questions.question: Through which channel are office alerts and parent confirmations delivered (in-app, push, e-mail, SMS), and who handles alerts if the office is unstaffed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Alert reliability is critical for the duty of care.

open_questions.question: Until what time on the same day may parents still report a sickness absence?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The cut-off time determines when an absence counts as unreported and triggers an alert.

assumptions: The pilot covers only Lindenhof primary school. A rollout to other schools is not part of this draft.
Teachers have school-provided tablets with internet access during lessons.
Parents can be reached through contact data held in the canton's student administration system.
Pupils with an approved planned absence or a reported absence are pre-marked in the attendance list, so teachers do not create false alerts.
The system replaces teachers' private phones as the channel for absence messages.
Office staff use a desktop computer for the overview and data entry.
out_of_scope: Collecting medical details or diagnoses about absences.
Manual entry or maintenance of student, class and parent master data in the absence system.
Translation into all of the school's more than twenty languages.
Automated phone calls to families. The office calls families itself after an alert.
Direct export to a report card system (not mentioned in the interview).
